title: Exploring the hub genes and potential drugs involved in Fanconi anemia using microarray datasets and bioinformatics analysis.
authors: Hameed, Alaa R; Fakhri Ali, Sama; N Almanaa, Taghreed; Aljasir, Mohammad Abdullah; Alruwetei, Abdulmohsen M; Sanami, Samira; Ayaz, Hassan; Ali, Ijaz; Ahmad, Faisal; Ahmad, Sajjad
one_liner_zh: 该文基于微阵列数据挖掘范可尼贫血枢纽基因并预测药物，仅涉及药物与TP53蛋白的分子对接和MD模拟，无蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: Fanconi anemia (FA) is a genetic disorder that occurs when certain genes responsible for repairing DNA replication and promoting homologous recombination fail to function properly. This leads to severe clinical symptoms and a wide range of cancer-related characteristics. Recent treatment approaches for FA involve hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT), which helps restore the population of stem cells. A survival study using p-values indicated that specific hub genes play a significant role in diagnosing and predicting the disease. To find potential medications that interact with the identified hub genes, researchers inferred drugs. Among hub genes, TP53 was found to be particularly promising through computational analysis. Further investigation focused on two drugs, Topiramate and Tocofersolan predicted based on drug bank database analysis. Molecular docking strategies were employed to assess the best binding pose of these drugs with TP53. Topiramate showed a binding affinity of -6.5 kcal/mol, while Tocofersolan showed -8.5 kcal/mol against the active residues within the binding pocket. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations were conducted to observe the stability of each drug's interaction with the TP53 protein over time. Both drugs exhibited stable confirmation with only slight changes in the loop region of the TP53 protein during the simulation intervals. Results also shows that there was a high fluctuation observed during apo-sate simulation time intervals as compared to complex system. Hence, it is suggested that the exploration of structure-based drug design holds promising results to specific target. This could potentially lead to a breakthrough in future experimental approaches for FA treatment.
abstract_zh: 范可尼贫血（Fanconi anemia, FA）是一种遗传性疾病，当负责修复DNA复制和促进同源重组（homologous recombination）的某些基因功能失常时发生。这导致严重的临床症状和广泛的癌症相关特征。目前FA的治疗方法涉及造血干细胞移植（hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, HSCT），有助于恢复干细胞群体。一项使用p值的生存研究表明，特定枢纽基因在诊断和预测该疾病中发挥重要作用。为寻找与已识别枢纽基因相互作用的潜在药物，研究人员推断出候选药物。在枢纽基因中，TP53通过计算分析被发现特别有前景。进一步研究聚焦于两种药物，即基于药物银行数据库分析预测的托吡酯（Topiramate）和生育酚聚乙二醇琥珀酸酯（Tocofersolan）。采用分子对接（molecular docking）策略评估这些药物与TP53的最佳结合构象。托吡酯对结合口袋内活性残基显示出-6.5 kcal/mol的结合亲和力，而托吡酯琥珀酸酯显示出-8.5 kcal/mol。进行了分子动力学（molecular dynamics, MD）模拟，以观察每种药物与TP53蛋白相互作用随时间变化的稳定性。两种药物均表现出稳定构象，在模拟间隔期间TP53蛋白的环区仅有轻微变化。结果还显示，与复合物系统相比，在无配体（apo-state）模拟时间间隔内观察到高波动。因此，建议基于结构的药物设计探索对特定靶点具有前景结果。这可能为未来FA治疗的实验方法带来突破。
